curriculum learning significantly improves the performance of reinforcement learning in the domain of proof guidance.

curriculum learning is a very effective technique in reinforcement learning for automated theorem proving, and that it is possible to generalize from short proofs to much longer ones of similar length and structure.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FLoP is a novel approach to automated theorem proving geared toward finding longer proofs by learning from previous proofs.
FLoP is the first approach to apply state-of-the-art reinforcement learning techniques for proof guidance.

the results of our experiments show that our approach is a promising direction towards finding longer proofs, but it is still far from being able to solve problems that cannot be solved by the underlying theorem prover.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of a good curriculum and the use of a powerful neural network architecture is key to improving the quality of proof guidance.

we are the first to show that RL-based techniques can be successfully applied in automated theorem proving and that curriculum learning significantly improves the performance of learning-based guidance.

the RL-based guidance system is able to find longer proofs than the state-of-the-art proof planning systems, and it is able to find proofs for problems that the state-of-the art systems are not able to solve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of RL and curriculum learning is a promising approach for finding longer proofs in automated theorem provers.
FLoP can learn to find proofs of longer length than previous work, and that the learned policies generalize to unseen problems of a similar structure.
RL-based guidance can be successfully applied in the context of FLoP, and that the FLoP approach itself is a promising direction for automated theorem proving.
